questions.question: How should a run decide the aaSlug for a new/changed provider model? Artificial Analysis lists many variants per model (e.g. 'GPT-5.6 Luna (low)', '(medium)', '(max)'), so fuzzy matching involves judgment.

options.label: Deterministic matcher (Recommended)
options.description: Normalize names/slugs into tokens and pick the unique AA model whose base name (qualifiers stripped) matches, preferring the plain slug. Ambiguous/no match → written as aaSlug: null with a note. No new deps or API keys.

options.label: LLM-assisted (Claude API)
options.description: Deterministic first, then ask Claude to resolve leftovers from a shortlist of AA candidates. Needs ANTHROPIC_API_KEY + @anthropic-ai/sdk; results may vary between runs.

options.label: Report only
options.description: Run just lists unmapped/broken entries and suggested slugs; a human edits the file.

questions.question: What should a run do with existing entries?

options.label: Fix only broken ones (Recommended)
options.description: Keep entries whose aaSlug still exists in AA data (manual choices and notes preserved). Re-match null entries and entries whose slug disappeared. Leave entries for models no longer offered.

options.label: Also prune stale
options.description: Same as above, plus remove entries for models no longer present in provider pricing.

options.label: Rematch everything
options.description: Recompute all entries every run; manual overrides are lost unless marked.

# Auto-update config/model-mapping.json during pipeline runs

## Context
`config/model-mapping.json` (provider model name → Artificial Analysis `aaSlug`) was written by hand/LLM on the first run. `src/index.ts:2` says it is "still maintained by hand". When providers add/rename models or AA renames slugs, `computeScores` just logs "no Artificial Analysis mapping" / "aaSlug not found" and silently drops the model. Goal: each run updates the mapping file itself — adding new models and fixing broken entries — using a deterministic matcher (no LLM, no new deps), while preserving existing valid manual choices and notes.

## Approach

### New module `src/mapping/update-mapping.ts` → `export async function updateModelMapping(): Promise<void>`
1. **Load inputs**
   - Provider candidates: reuse `loadCandidates()` from `src/scoring/compute-scores.ts` (export it; it already dedupes tiered rows via `baseModelName`, so names match mapping keys like `"Qwen3.8 Max"`). Don't apply the blacklist — mapping blacklisted models is harmless.
   - AA models from `data/artificial-analysis/language-models.json` (reuse/export the `AaModel` type).
   - Existing `config/model-mapping.json` (extend `MappingEntry` with optional `note`; move the type to the new module or a shared spot and import it in compute-scores).

2. **Build AA index** (key → chosen slug)
   - Key = token set of the AA name with trailing `(...)` qualifiers stripped (reuse `baseModelName`): lowercase, split on non-alphanumerics, sort, join. E.g. `"Claude 4.5 Haiku (Reasoning)"` → `4 5 claude haiku`; `"MiMo-V2.5"` → `5 mimo v2`.
   - Group AA models by key; pick the **shortest slug** in the group (AA's base variant has the unsuffixed slug: `gpt-5-6-luna` vs `gpt-5-6-luna-low`, `claude-4-5-haiku` vs `-reasoning`). If the shortest isn't a prefix of the others / ties → mark ambiguous.

3. **Reconcile each candidate** (provider + model)
   - Existing entry with non-null `aaSlug` that exists in AA data → **keep untouched** (manual choices like `muse-spark-1-3` for "Contributor" stay).
   - Existing entry with `aaSlug: null`, or slug no longer in AA data → re-match; if a unique match is found, set `aaSlug` and drop the note; otherwise leave `aaSlug: null` with a note (e.g. `"Auto: no Artificial Analysis match (last checked <date>)."` or `"previous slug X disappeared"`). Don't overwrite a hand-written null note when nothing changed.
   - No entry → append new entry (matched slug, or `null` + auto note).
   - Entries for models no longer offered → left as-is.

4. **Write back only if changed**, in the file's current style: one JSON object per line, existing order kept, new entries appended at the end of their provider group, blank line between provider groups. Log a summary: `added N, updated M, unmatched K` with per-model lines for changes.

### Pipeline wiring — `src/index.ts`
- Insert `== Step 4/5: updating model mapping ==` calling `updateModelMapping()` after the AA fetch and before scoring (renumber steps to /5).
- Replace the header comment "still maintained by hand -- see README" with a note that the mapping is auto-updated and manual edits to valid entries are preserved.

### Docs
- `README.md`: short section on `config/model-mapping.json` — auto-maintained each run; to override, set `aaSlug` by hand (kept as long as the slug exists in AA data); `null` entries are retried every run.

## Critical files
- `src/mapping/update-mapping.ts` (new)
- `src/scoring/compute-scores.ts` — export `loadCandidates`, `baseModelName`, `AaModel`/`MappingEntry` types
- `src/index.ts` — new step
- `README.md`

## Verification
1. Offline dry check using existing local data (no network): `node --input-type=module -e "import('./src/mapping/update-mapping.ts').then(m => m.updateModelMapping())"` — with the current file, expect **no changes** except possibly re-resolved null entries (e.g. "Qwen3.8 Flash" should stay null since only `qwen3-8-flash-next` exists). `git diff config/model-mapping.json` should be empty or minimal.
2. Simulate additions: temporarily delete a few lines (e.g. "Claude Haiku 4.5", "GPT 5.6 Luna", "MiMo V2.5") and rerun → they come back with `claude-4-5-haiku`, `gpt-5-6-luna`, `mimo-v2-5-0424`. Change one slug to a bogus value → it gets repaired. Restore with `git checkout config/model-mapping.json`.
3. `npm run lint` and `npm run format`.
4. Full `npm start` → step 4 logs the summary, step 5 scoring has no new "no Artificial Analysis mapping" warnings for matchable models.

When providers add/rename models or AA renames slugs, `computeScores` just logs "no Artificial Analysis mapping" / "aaSlug not found" and silently drops the model. Goal: each run updates the mapping file itself — adding new models and fixing broken entries — using a deterministic matcher (no LLM, no new deps), while preserving existing valid manual choices and notes.

## Approach

2. **Build AA index** (key → chosen slug)

Every run now updates `config/model-mapping.json` itself, as a new step before scoring. I tested it offline against the local data but haven't done a full `npm start` with a live fetch.

**How it works** ([update-mapping.ts](src/mapping/update-mapping.ts))
- **Matching:** provider models are matched to Artificial Analysis by name. Word order is ignored, and so are qualifiers like `(Reasoning)` or `(max)`. So "Claude Haiku 4.5" matches "Claude 4.5 Haiku (Reasoning)".
- **Picking a variant:** AA lists one entry per effort level. The updater picks the plain slug (`gpt-5-6-luna`, not `gpt-5-6-luna-low`). If there's no clear plain slug, it writes `aaSlug: null` with a note instead of guessing.
- **Entries whose slug exists in AA data are never changed**, so your hand-picked slugs and notes stay put.
- **Null entries and entries whose slug is gone from AA data** are matched again on every run.
- **New models** go at the end of their provider's group. The file keeps its one-entry-per-line layout, and it's only written when something changed.

**First run on your data** made two real changes, and I checked both against the AA data:
- `Claude Opus 4.8`: `null` → `claude-opus-4-8`. The old note said AA didn't track it, but it does now.
- `MiniMax M2.5` was added as `minimax-m2-5`. It's a new OpenCode Go model.

The rest of the file is unchanged byte for byte. Three models still have no match: "Qwen3.8 Flash", "MAI-Code-1.1-Flash" and "Hy4 preview".

**Test:** I deleted the Haiku 4.5, GPT 5.6 Luna and MiMo V2.5 entries and gave Qwen3.8 Max a fake slug. One run put all four back with the right slugs, and then I restored the file.

**Other changes**
- [index.ts](src/index.ts) now has 5 steps.
- [compute-scores.ts](src/scoring/compute-scores.ts) now exports `loadCandidates`, `baseModelName` and the types so the updater can reuse them.
- The [README](README.md) has a short section on how the mapping is maintained.

Lint and formatting pass on the changed files. `oxfmt --check src` also flags 6 files I didn't touch. That's only because they have Windows (CRLF) line endings in your working copy (`core.autocrlf=true`); the committed files are fine.

Nothing is committed yet.
